effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood model and showed that blood carries defenders and parts needed to seal leaks as well as materials.
reaction: The cutaway was helpful for seeing the difference between oxygen in red cells and nutrients in plasma.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to the red cells was most worthwhile: the paired arrows showed that oxygen can attach and then leave near tissues, not just ride permanently in the blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the components to plasma in two separate steps felt predictable, although the outlines made the order easy to follow.

surprise.text: I was interested that the mature red cells had no nuclei, even though the developing cells started with them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though choosing red cells before white cells and platelets was mainly an order choice rather than a clear biological decision.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how blood delivers its materials around the body. The oxygen attachment and release made me curious, even though the assembly steps were fairly predictable.
